subjects.label: Handling and messing with objects
subjects.description: Picking up, throwing, smashing, poking and drawing on the things in the world, and the small physical details of the objects themselves; not combat or puzzle mechanics as systems.

subjects.label: Hopes for a sequel and the wait
subjects.description: Wanting the series to continue and reckoning with the wait: the next instalment, the numbered sequel this is not, and another decade of silence; not a verdict on this game itself.

subjects.label: Place in the series
subjects.description: The game as an entry in a long-running series: fans of the earlier games, a return to its roots, and people who never liked the series before; not the plot of this game on its own.

subjects.label: The studio's reputation
subjects.description: Praise, faith or worry aimed at the developer as a studio, its founder and its golden age, rather than at anything this game does; post-release patching belongs in updates.

subjects.label: The VR showcase
subjects.description: The game as the reason to own a headset, the best thing yet made for VR and what it did for the medium and headset sales; comfort, tracking and which headset works belong in vr.

subjects.label: Physical toll of playing
subjects.description: What playing does to the body and the room: exhaustion, sweating, and hitting the desk or the wardrobe while in the headset; motion sickness and comfort settings stay in vr.

subjects.label: Enemies and creatures
subjects.description: The particular creatures players remember, whether they scared, annoyed or amused them, named by kind or by the chapter they haunt; not the story characters or the combat system.
